summary: Environment A direct-binary proof that Phase 11 (Local Congregant Companion View) compiled into the real Windows NSIS installer: the companion HTTP server, its three new Tauri commands, and its served JSON/HTML content are all present in the shipped exe, with zero regression against every prior phase's symbol tripwires.

installer.ggmlTwoPassFixNote: First build attempt failed as expected on the known whisper-rs-sys ggml lib-name defect; the build script applied its established fix and the retry succeeded - the same harmless, unrelated build-toolchain quirk documented and handled identically in every prior whisper-enabled Windows rebuild this project has done.

symbolRegressionCheck.method: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings cip-desktop.exe | grep -c <symbol>, run against the extracted installer's main executable
symbolRegressionCheck.tripwiresResult: All 10 counts identical to the Phase 10 baseline - zero regression. whisper_full_with_state stable at 96 for a 5th consecutive rebuild (Phase 7.3 through Phase 11).
symbolRegressionCheck.phase8Phase9Phase10Note: Every prior-phase symbol checked (Production Integration, Bible Translation Registry v2, Church/User Roles & Permissions) remains present and unregressed.

newSymbolsNote: Direct strings inspection shows the exact literal command names in the Tauri invoke_handler registration list (...list_operator_accounts...enable_congregant_companion...disable_congregant_companion...get_congregant_companion_status...get_pilot_diagnostics...), the CompanionSnapshot/status JSON field names (active, heading, bodyLines, footer, updatedAt), both mutex-poisoned panic messages (companion_snapshot mutex poisoned, companion_server mutex poisoned) carrying the source path apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/companion.rs, the UDP routing-table-trick addresses (0.0.0.0:0, 8.8.8.8:80) used by detect_local_ip, the operator-facing log lines (congregant companion server enabled/disabled on port), and the served page's own localStorage key (cip-companion-notes) and notes-disclosure copy (saved only on your phone) - comprehensive, unambiguous direct proof this phase's server, commands, and served content all compiled into and shipped inside the real Windows executable. CompanionStatusDto (the Rust type name itself, never embedded as a string literal) and the literal port number 49876 (a numeric immediate, not ASCII text, so invisible to `strings`) both show 0 occurrences - the same 'not found as a string, not evidence of absence' pattern already documented for small helper names and constants in every prior phase's own installer-contents-verification.json.
frontendTextSearchLimitation: The frontend bundle (dist/assets/index-*.js) is bundled into the Tauri resources directory, not searchable as plain strings inside cip-desktop.exe itself in the same way Rust symbols are - CongregantCompanionPanel.tsx's own UI copy was not independently string-searched in this phase, consistent with every prior phase's installer-contents-verification methodology in this project. This phase's frontend correctness rests on npm run typecheck's success, the fresh Vite build hash, and the full 280/280 frontend test pass.
architecturalSafetyNotes: 3 new Tauri commands, zero new events, zero new migrations - no persistence at all.

The two companion::update_snapshot call sites (visible in the strings output immediately beside test_obs_connection/production-related strings) sit alongside production::push_to_configured_targets's own existing calls, unchanged.
generate_verse_embeddings, ensure_admin, and every Phase 8/9/10 command remain present and unregressed, confirming this phase's additions did not disturb any prior gate.
environmentCStatus: Not yet performed. A real operator on real Windows hardware enabling the companion server and a real phone on the same LAN opening the served page and confirming it tracks Stage live (displaying and clearing items) is required to close Environment C for this phase, exactly as for every prior phase's physicalHardwareStatement discipline.
